report.summary: One Deployment (search-api) has a pod in CrashLoopBackOff due to failing liveness probes; the owning Deployment is available but has 0 ready replicas.

incidents.root_cause: The Deployment’s liveness probe is misconfigured and is probing the container on port 8080 using a combined path/port string ("/:8080") with a very short initialDelaySeconds (3s). Nginx in the container starts on its default port (80), so the probe’s HTTP GET to 10.244.0.12:8080 is refused; kubelet kills and restarts the container, causing CrashLoopBackOff.

evidence.detail: pod search-api-6c89bcf949-898jk: container "api" ready=false, restart_count=2, state=waiting, reason=CrashLoopBackOff, message='back-off 10s restarting failed container=api'.

Event Warning Unhealthy: 'Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.0.12:8080/": dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused' (count: 6). Also 'Container api failed liveness probe, will be restarted'.

Container logs show nginx started (noting 'nginx/1.27.5' and 'start worker processes') and then the master received SIGQUIT and exited shortly after ('signal 3 (SIGQUIT) received, shutting down'). This is consistent with kubelet killing the process after failed liveness probes.

Deployment search-api liveness probe: handler=http, target='/:8080', initial_delay_seconds=3, period_seconds=3, timeout_seconds=1, failure_threshold=2 (from describe_workload). No readiness or startup probe configured.
Pod owner chain: ReplicaSet 'search-api-6c89bcf949' -> Deployment 'search-api' (owning workload: Deployment search-api).

proposed_actions.description: Fix the liveness probe to target the correct HTTP path and port and give the container more startup time. Change the probe to httpGet.path='/' and httpGet.port=80 (or the container port nginx listens on), increase initialDelaySeconds to 10–30s, increase periodSeconds to 10 and failureThreshold to 3 so transient startup delays don't trigger restarts.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl -n search patch deployment search-api --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe","value":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":15,"periodSeconds":10,"timeoutSeconds":1,"failureThreshold":3}}]'

proposed_actions.description: After patching the probe, trigger a rollout restart to ensure all pods pick up the change and to recover availability quickly.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl -n search rollout restart deployment/search-api

proposed_actions.description: Verify the change and observe pod status and events. If the container intentionally listens on a non-default port, alternatively update the container configuration to listen on the probed port. Confirm logs no longer show repeated SIGQUIT and that liveness events stop.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl -n search describe deployment search-api && kubectl -n search get pods -w && kubectl -n search get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=search-api-6c89bcf949-898jk | tail -n +1

incidents.judge_reasoning: The diagnosis identifies all key facts: the liveness probe targets port 8080 while nginx serves on port 80, resulting in connection refused and repeated kubelet restarts. The proposed patch changes the probe port to 80, fixing the root cause; the additional timing adjustments, restart, and verification steps are not harmful.

report.summary: Deployment docs-site had transient readiness probe failures (connection refused) during container startup; the workload remains available but kubelet logged Unhealthy events for two pods. Root cause is readiness probe configuration (no initialDelay, 1s timeout) causing probes to hit before nginx bound. Recommend adding an initialDelay or startupProbe and then rolling the deployment.

incidents.root_cause: Readiness probe begins immediately (initialDelay not set) with timeoutSeconds=1 and failureThreshold=3, so kubelet probed the container before nginx had finished binding the port, producing transient “connection refused” readiness failures. The Deployment spec shows readinessProbe: handler=http target=/:80 initial_delay_seconds=null period_seconds=10 timeout_seconds=1 failure_threshold=3 (and container requests cpu=10m memory=32Mi, limits memory=64Mi).

evidence.detail: Warning Unhealthy: "Readiness probe failed: Get \"http://10.244.0.8:80/\": dial tcp 10.244.0.8:80: connect: connection refused" (pod docs-site-584dbd4fcd-448xm) and similar for docs-site-584dbd4fcd-r4fpb.
Deployment docs-site readiness probe: handler=http target=/:80 initial_delay_seconds=null period_seconds=10 timeout_seconds=1 failure_threshold=3; requests: cpu=10m memory=32Mi; limits: memory=64Mi.

Pod docs-site-584dbd4fcd-448xm logs: nginx startup completed and shows kube-probe requests returning 200 (e.g. "10.244.0.1 - - [14/Oct/2026:11:37:17 +0000] \"GET / HTTP/1.1\" 200 615 \"-\" \"kube-probe/1.37\" \"-\"").

Pod docs-site-584dbd4fcd-r4fpb logs: nginx startup completed and shows kube-probe requests returning 200 shortly after startup (e.g. "10.244.0.1 - - [14/Oct/2026:11:37:15 +0000] \"GET / HTTP/1.1\" 200 615 \"-\" \"kube-probe/1.37\" \"-\"").
Pod docs-site-584dbd4fcd-448xm is owned by ReplicaSet docs-site-584dbd4fcd -> Deployment docs-site.
list_pods returned total=0 unhealthy when queried with only_unhealthy=true, indicating pods were not persistently failing at the time of the check.

proposed_actions.description: Give the readiness probe time to avoid probing before nginx binds: set initialDelaySeconds (e.g. 5–10s) and increase timeoutSeconds to 2s. This prevents transient connection-refused readiness events without changing app behavior.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl patch deployment docs-site -n website --type='strategic' --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"web","readinessProbe":{"initialDelaySeconds":10,"timeoutSeconds":2}}]}}}}'

proposed_actions.description: Alternatively (preferred for apps that may take variable time to start), add a startupProbe so readiness/liveness probes don't run until the app is healthy. Example: HTTP startupProbe on / port 80 with longer failureThreshold and periodSeconds.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl patch deployment docs-site -n website --type='strategic' --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"web","startupProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"periodSeconds":10,"failureThreshold":30}}]}}}}'

proposed_actions.description: After patching the probe settings, restart pods to pick up the change and verify behavior.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl rollout restart deployment/docs-site -n website && kubectl rollout status deployment/docs-site -n website

report.summary: One Deployment (order-worker) has a single pod crashing on startup due to an application bug (ZeroDivisionError). Pod repeatedly restarts and is in BackOff; Deployment has 1 desired replica but 0 ready/available.

incidents.root_cause: The worker process divides by the number of loaded shards without handling the case where the shard map is empty. The container prints "shards loaded: 0" then raises a ZeroDivisionError (total // len(shards)). The Deployment has no resource requests/limits and no liveness/readiness/startup probes configured (so kubelet just restarts the failing container until BackOff).

evidence.detail: Traceback... ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero; logs also show 'order-worker 2.4.1 starting' and 'shards loaded: 0' (container worker crashed).
Warning BackOff: 'Back-off restarting failed container worker in pod order-worker-7dbdc597df-9tx6b_orders(...)' and Normal events: Pulled/Created/Started (kubelet retried then backed off).

Deployment order-worker spec shows container image 'python:3.11-slim' and command is an inline python -c script that computes orders_per_shard using 'return total // len(shards)'; liveness/readiness/startup are null and requests/limits are empty.
Pod order-worker-7dbdc597df-9tx6b: phase=Running, container 'worker' not ready, restart_count=2, last_termination exit_code=1 (Error).
Pod owner chain: ReplicaSet order-worker-7dbdc597df -> Deployment order-worker (owning workload).

proposed_actions.description: Fix the application to handle an empty shard map (avoid division by zero). Update the code so orders_per_shard returns 0 or uses a safe default when len(shards)==0, and add proper error handling and logging. Rebuild the container image and push to your registry.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: (developer) Update code; build and push image, e.g. 'docker build -t registry.example.com/order-worker:fix . && docker push registry.example.com/order-worker:fix'.

proposed_actions.description: Deploy the fixed image to replace the crashing container once the image is published. This replaces the faulty code and will stop the crash loop.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl set image deployment/order-worker worker=registry.example.com/order-worker:fix -n orders

proposed_actions.description: Add startup/readiness (and optionally liveness) probes so Kubernetes can distinguish startup failures from runtime failures, and add resource requests/limits to make scheduling and OOM behavior explicit. Example: add a startupProbe that waits for successful initialization before marking the pod ready, and a readinessProbe for steady-state health.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl patch deployment order-worker -n orders --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/startupProbe","value":{"exec":{"command":["/bin/sh","-c","python -c \"import sys; sys.exit(0)\""]},"failureThreshold":30,"periodSeconds":5}},{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe","value":{"exec":{"command":["/bin/sh","-c","python -c \"import sys; sys.exit(0)\""]},"initialDelaySeconds":5,"periodSeconds":10}}]'

proposed_actions.description: As an immediate safety measure you can patch the Deployment's command to a guarded version that prevents division-by-zero while you rebuild the image (short-term mitigation). Replace the inline python -c with a version that checks for zero shards before dividing.
After deploying the fixed image or patching the command, restart the Deployment to pick up the change and clear the CrashLoopBackOff state.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl rollout restart deployment/order-worker -n orders

incidents.judge_reasoning: The diagnosis correctly identifies the startup ZeroDivisionError caused by dividing by len(shards) when the shard map is empty. Fixing the application and deploying the rebuilt image would address the cause, but the temporary command override merely prints and exits rather than running the worker, and the proposed probes always succeed without checking application health. These problematic additions make the remediation a correct fix mixed with harmful changes.

report.summary: 1 deployment (notifier) has a pod stuck in init due to its initContainer failing DNS lookups for the database service, preventing the pod from becoming ready.

incidents.root_cause: The initContainer wait-for-db exits with code 1 because it cannot resolve the service hostname notifications-db (DNS NXDOMAIN). This prevents the init container from completing, so the main container never starts and the Deployment has no available replicas. The notifier Deployment has no probes and uses image nginx:1.27-alpine for the main container; the initContainer uses busybox and is exiting immediately on DNS failure.

...

** server can't find notifications-db.notifications.svc.cluster.local: NXDOMAIN

proposed_actions.description: Check whether the notifications-db Service/Pod/StatefulSet exists and restore or create it if missing. The init container is failing DNS lookups for notifications-db, so bringing the DB service back or creating the correct Service name will allow the init container to succeed.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl get svc notifications-db -n notifications || echo 'service not found'; kubectl get pods,deploy,statefulset -l app=notifications-db -n notifications; # if missing: kubectl apply -f notifications-db-manifest.yaml -n notifications

proposed_actions.description: If the DB exists under a different name or is external, update the notifier Deployment's initContainer to point to the correct hostname or add a robust wait loop (retry with sleep) instead of failing immediately. This avoids NXDOMAIN failure causing the initContainer to exit with code 1.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl -n notifications patch deployment notifier --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/initContainers/0/command","value":["/bin/sh","-c","until nslookup notifications-db.notifications.svc.cluster.local >/dev/null 2>&1; do echo waiting for DB; sleep 5; done"]}]' # then kubectl rollout status deploy/notifier -n notifications

proposed_actions.description: After fixing the database Service/hostname or patching the initContainer, restart the Deployment so pods re-run the fixed initContainer and reach ready state.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl rollout restart deployment/notifier -n notifications && kubectl rollout status deployment/notifier -n notifications

incidents.judge_reasoning: The diagnosis correctly identifies wait-for-db failing because notifications-db cannot resolve, preventing init completion and the main container from starting. Creating or restoring the Service or correcting the hostname fixes the root cause; the retry loop and restart alone would not, but they do not make the proposed remediation harmful.

report.summary: One Deployment (invoice-service) has a pod stuck Pending due to a missing key in a referenced Secret, preventing containers from being created.

incidents.root_cause: The Deployment’s container environment references Secret "billing-db" keys (DB_USER -> username, DB_PASSWORD -> password) but the key "password" is missing from the Secret in namespace billing. Kubernetes reports CreateContainerConfigError because it cannot resolve the secret key, so the container is never started.

Event: Warning Failed: "Error: couldn't find key password in Secret billing/billing-db" (kubelet events for the Pod).
Workload spec: Deployment invoice-service env entries: DB_USER from Secret billing-db key 'username', DB_PASSWORD from Secret billing-db key 'password' (from describe_workload).
Pod owner chain: Pod -> ReplicaSet invoice-service-774dd578 -> Deployment invoice-service (ownership resolution).

proposed_actions.description: Inspect the secret to confirm which keys exist, and add the missing 'password' key (or correct the secret name). This fixes the CreateContainerConfigError by providing the secret data the pod expects.

kubectl get secret billing-db -n billing -o yaml
# If 'password' is missing, create or update the secret (example creates a new secret):
kubectl create secret generic billing-db --from-literal=username=<username> --from-literal=password='<password>' -n billing
# Or patch an existing secret with a base64 value for 'password' if you prefer (advanced).

proposed_actions.suggested_command:
kubectl edit deployment invoice-service -n billing
# In the Pod template, set the secretKeyRef block to include 'optional: true' for DB_PASSWORD, then save to apply.

proposed_actions.description: After fixing the Secret or patching the Deployment, restart the Deployment so the pod(s) are re-created with the corrected config.
proposed_actions.suggested_command:
kubectl rollout restart deployment/invoice-service -n billing
kubectl get pods -n billing -w

report.summary: 1 failing workload: Deployment search-api is CrashLoopBackOff due to liveness probe failures (probing port 8080 while nginx listens on port 80) causing repeated restarts.

nginx started (2026/10/14 11:37:42 ... start worker processes) then received signal 3 (SIGQUIT) and exited at 2026/10/14 11:37:48 - indicates the process was asked to stop by the container runtime or kubelet.

Warning Unhealthy: 'Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.0.12:8080/": dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused'; Normal Killing: 'Container api failed liveness probe, will be restarted'.
Pod search-api-6c89bcf949-898jk: container 'api' ready=false, restart_count=2, state=waiting (CrashLoopBackOff).
Pod owned by ReplicaSet search-api-6c89bcf949 -> Deployment search-api.

proposed_actions.description: Patch the Deployment's liveness probe to target the container's actual listening port (80) and relax probe timings to avoid premature restarts. This fixes the connection refused errors by probing the correct port and reduces false positives.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl patch deployment search-api -n search --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe","value":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80},"initialDelaySeconds":10,"periodSeconds":5,"timeoutSeconds":2,"failureThreshold":3}}]'

proposed_actions.description: After patching the probe, restart the Deployment to ensure all pods pick up the change and recover from CrashLoopBackOff.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl rollout restart deployment/search-api -n search

proposed_actions.description: If the intention was for the application to listen on port 8080 instead of 80, change the container configuration (image/command) so the process binds to 8080, and then keep or adjust the probe accordingly. Also consider updating container ports in the Pod spec.
proposed_actions.suggested_command: kubectl edit deployment search-api -n search  # modify container args or image to listen on 8080, or adjust probes as needed

proposed_actions.description: After remediation, monitor pod events and logs to confirm: 'kubectl get pods -n search', 'kubectl describe pod <pod> -n search', and 'kubectl logs -n search <pod> -c api --previous' to verify the probe succeeds and restarts stop.

Patching the probe to port 80 fixes the root cause; the timing adjustments, restart, monitoring, and conditional alternative configuration do not introduce a harmful action.

report.summary: One StatefulSet (inventory-db) cannot start: its Pod is Pending because the PVC is stuck Pending due to a missing StorageClass (fast-ssd).

incidents.root_cause: The StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplate requested storageClassName 'fast-ssd' but that StorageClass does not exist in the cluster, so the PVC 'data-inventory-db-0' is Pending and the pod remains unschedulable.

evidence.detail: Pod inventory-db-0 is owned by StatefulSet inventory-db.
Pod inventory-db-0 phase=Pending; failing_conditions: 'PodScheduled: Unschedulable - 0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims. not found'.
PersistentVolumeClaim data-inventory-db-0 status=Pending, storage_class='fast-ssd', requested='1Gi'.
Warning ProvisioningFailed: 'storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found' for PVC data-inventory-db-0.
Warning FailedScheduling: '0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims. not found' for Pod inventory-db-0.

StatefulSet inventory-db spec: desired=1, ready=0; container 'db' image='nginx:1.27-alpine'; volumeClaimTemplates referenced storageClassName='fast-ssd' (in PVC data-inventory-db-0). Requests/limits/probes: none set.

proposed_actions.description: Create or restore a StorageClass named 'fast-ssd' (or create a StorageClass that satisfies the PVC) so the PVC can be provisioned and bound. This fixes the ProvisioningFailed event and allows the StatefulSet to create a PV and start the Pod.
proposed_actions.suggested_command:
kubectl get storageclass && kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd
provisioner: <your-storage-provisioner>
parameters:
  type: gp3
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
EOF
# Replace <your-storage-provisioner> and parameters with a provisioner available in your cluster (e.g. ebs.csi.aws.com, pd.csi.storage.gke.io).

proposed_actions.description: If you cannot or do not want to create 'fast-ssd', edit the StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplates to reference an existing StorageClass (e.g. 'standard'), then delete the stuck PVC so the StatefulSet will recreate it with the new storageClassName. Editing the StatefulSet updates the template for future replicas.
proposed_actions.suggested_command:
kubectl get storageclass && kubectl edit statefulset inventory-db -n inventory
# In the editor, set spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].spec.storageClassName to an existing class (e.g. 'standard').
# Then remove the stuck PVC so it can be recreated:
kubectl delete pvc data-inventory-db-0 -n inventory
# The StatefulSet will recreate the PVC using the updated template.

proposed_actions.description: As a short-term workaround, create a PersistentVolume that matches the PVC (name, size, accessModes) and bind it to the claim, if dynamic provisioning is unavailable. This will allow the Pod to schedule immediately.
proposed_actions.suggested_command:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-data-inventory-db-0
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  claimRef:
    namespace: inventory
    name: data-inventory-db-0
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data/inventory-db-0  # example for single-node clusters; replace with appropriate backend
EOF
# Adjust spec to match your environment (NFS, cloud PV, etc.).

incidents.judge_reasoning: The diagnosis correctly identifies the missing fast-ssd StorageClass, the resulting Pending PVC, and the pod's inability to schedule because the claim is unbound. Creating fast-ssd with an available provisioner fixes the root cause. The alternative StatefulSet edit would fail because volumeClaimTemplates is immutable, but the valid primary fix is sufficient and the other actions do not clearly worsen the incident.

report.summary: One Deployment (profile-web) has a single pod that is Running but not Ready due to failing readiness probes; the container is up (nginx) but probes request /healthz which is not served, causing the Deployment to have 0 available replicas.
